newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Bombs blast Algiers, five dead, about 50 wounded.
newsitem.headline: Bombs blast Algiers, five dead, about 50 wounded.

text.p: Two bombs exploded in Algiers on Sunday, one ripping through a crowded bus and killing five people, including a baby, just days before Algeria's first general election after more than five years of bloodshed.
Security forces said the first bomb, in Martyrs' Square in the heart of the capital, went off around 4 p.m. (1500 GMT).
Witnesses said the bomb also wounded about 30 people on the crowded bus.
"It was full of workers heading home and the bomb went off just before it left the bus station," one witnesses said.
Police quickly ringed the area as ambulances, sirens screaming, raced to and from the scene, bathed in bright sunlight.
The second bomb went off in Gharmoul Street, in another part of the city centre, wounding between 15 and 20 people, another witness said.
The street houses the headquarters of the civil protection service, responsible for rescue work in such attacks. The blast was heard 1.5 km away by guests in the Aurassi Hotel.
On Thursday, Algeria holds a general elections which the authorities hope will help end years of bloodshed which they blame on Moslem fundamentalists.

Security forces blamed Moslem rebels for the blast at Martyrs' Square, using the term "criminal act" -- the authorities' official shorthand for violence for which they hold fundamentalists responsible.
On Saturday, a bomb exploded in a cinema in the Algerian capital. Officials said five people were wounded, two seriously. An Algerian newspaper on Sunday put the toll at one dead and 24 wounded.
About 60,000 people have been killed in violence since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Moslem fundamentalists had taken a commanding lead.
